providers.action.install.note: Provider Setup's button: installs the coding agent's CLI in a terminal.

providers.action.signIn.note: Provider Setup's button: signs the coding agent's CLI in, in a terminal.

providers.action.update.note: Provider Setup's button: updates the coding agent's CLI in a terminal.

providers.antigravity.checkFailed.text: Couldn't check {provider}'s sign-in: {text}. Choose Check again; if you haven't signed in yet, run agy in a terminal.
providers.antigravity.checkFailed.note: Provider Setup, under Antigravity CLI, when listing its models failed for a reason other than a known sign-in error (a network or service error, a timeout). {provider} is its name, {text} the CLI's own words (not translated). agy is a command: keep it; Check again is a button.

providers.antigravity.conversationGone.text: {provider} didn't resume {conversation}: {provider} no longer has that conversation (it keeps it apart from its transcript, in the agent's profile, and it was removed). Start a new session instead.
providers.antigravity.conversationGone.note: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't resume a conversation (its pane): the conversation's own store in the agent's profile is gone, though its transcript may be left. {provider} is the CLI's name, {conversation} the conversation's id.

providers.antigravity.notOwnConversation.text: {provider} didn't resume {conversation}: it isn't in this agent's own conversations (it may have been removed, or be another agent's). Start a new session instead.
providers.antigravity.notOwnConversation.note: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't resume a conversation (its pane): the conversation isn't among this agent's own. {provider} is the CLI's name, {conversation} the conversation's id.

providers.antigravity.projectServers.text: {provider} didn't start: {count, plural, one {{files} defines} other {{files} define}} MCP servers this agent wasn't given ({servers}), and {provider} would start them in its session. Combwork can't keep them out, so it doesn't start {provider} here. Remove them from that file, or give them to the agent in Combwork's MCP servers.
providers.antigravity.projectServers.note: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't start (its pane): a project or added folder's .agents config defines MCP servers the agent wasn't given, which Antigravity can't be kept from starting. {provider} is the CLI's name, {files} the config files' paths joined as a list, {count} how many files, {servers} the servers' names joined as a list. MCP servers is a place in Combwork.

providers.antigravity.setup.action.note: Provider Setup's button: opens Antigravity CLI's first-run screens in a terminal.

providers.antigravity.setup.copied.text: Each Antigravity agent then starts past those screens: Combwork copies only that they are done into its private profile, never your own Antigravity settings.
providers.antigravity.setup.copied.note: Provider Setup, under Antigravity CLI's Set up: what Combwork does with it.

providers.antigravity.setup.needed.text: Antigravity needs a one-time setup: its first-run screens. Until then each new agent shows them in its pane.
providers.antigravity.setup.needed.note: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: Antigravity CLI's first-run screens (a colour scheme, its terms of service) aren't done yet.

providers.antigravity.setup.runs.text: **Set up** runs `agy` in a terminal: choose a colour scheme and read and accept its terms there, its data-use choice yours. Combwork types nothing into it, and closes it once you are done.
providers.antigravity.setup.runs.note: Provider Setup, under Antigravity CLI's Set up: what it does. **…** marks bold text and `…` a command: keep the marks and the command.

providers.antigravity.unreadableConfig.text: {provider} didn't start: Combwork couldn't read {file} ({why}), which it would load. Fix or remove the file, then start the agent again.
providers.antigravity.unreadableConfig.note: Why an Antigravity CLI agent didn't start (its pane): a config file in the project (an MCP server or hook list) couldn't be read, so Combwork couldn't keep what it holds out of the agent. {provider} is the CLI's name, {file} a path, {why} the error's own words.

providers.claude.localLimits.outputNotBe.text: {agent} wasn’t started: its output budget ({output, number} tokens, {outputFrom}) isn’t below its context size ({context, number} tokens, {contextFrom}). Change one of them, then start it again.
providers.claude.localLimits.outputNotBe.note: An error starting an agent on a local model (HI-2682): the output budget Claude Code would get isn't smaller than its context. {agent} is the agent's name; {output} and {context} are numbers of tokens; {outputFrom} and {contextFrom} say where each was set ("Context size on Local", "env in the project's .claude/settings.json").

providers.claude.localLimits.tooSmall.text: {agent} wasn’t started: its context size ({context, number} tokens, {contextFrom}) is too small for any output budget. Set a larger context size.
providers.claude.localLimits.tooSmall.note: An error starting an agent on a local model (HI-2682): its context is so small that no output budget fits. {agent} is the agent's name; {context} is a number of tokens; {contextFrom} says where it was set.

providers.cmdTooLong.text: {file} has to run through cmd.exe, which takes a command line of at most {max, number} characters, and this launch needs about {length, number}. Set the CLI's path in Settings to its .exe (or install the standalone CLI), which has no such limit.
providers.cmdTooLong.note: Starting an agent is refused: its CLI is a .cmd or .bat launcher, and cmd.exe can't take a command line this long. {file} is the launcher's file name; {max} and {length} are numbers of characters. Keep cmd.exe and .exe as they are.

providers.codex.nativeCombwork.text: Your Codex config has an MCP server named combwork, reached over HTTP ({file}). Codex merges it into Combwork’s own combwork server, and can’t start with both. Rename yours there to start Codex agents.
providers.codex.nativeCombwork.note: Why a Codex agent didn't start: the user's own Codex config has an MCP server named combwork. {file} is that config file's path. combwork is the name of Combwork's MCP server (HI-2463): keep it.

providers.codex.sandbox.needed.text: Codex needs a one-time setup of its Windows sandbox; until then it asks before every command.
providers.codex.sandbox.needed.note: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: Codex's Windows sandbox isn't set up yet.

providers.codex.sandbox.nonAdminUsed.note: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: Codex runs commands in its non-admin sandbox (Windows), which can be upgraded.

providers.codex.sandbox.setUpAction.note: Provider Setup's button: opens Codex's sandbox setup in a terminal.

providers.codex.sandbox.upgrade.text: **Upgrade** switches Codex to its default sandbox, which runs commands under separate Windows accounts instead of your own. Windows asks for Administrator permission once. Codex agents that are running keep their sandbox until they restart.
providers.codex.sandbox.upgrade.note: Provider Setup, under Codex's sandbox setup (Windows): what Upgrade does. **…** marks bold text: keep the marks.

providers.codex.sandbox.upgradeAction.note: Provider Setup's button: switches Codex to its default sandbox.

providers.codex.storePwsh.fix.text: To avoid it, replace the Store's PowerShell 7 with the installer's, in this order. First uninstall the Store one (Settings → Apps → Installed apps → PowerShell → Uninstall, or `Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell | Remove-AppxPackage`): while it is there, winget takes it for the same app and installs nothing. Then install PowerShell 7 (`winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget --installer-type wix`). Then restart Combwork and its Codex agents: they keep their old PATH until they restart. Combwork leaves your shell as it is.
providers.codex.storePwsh.fix.note: Provider Setup (#585, #1512), under the warning about the Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7: what to do, in an order that must stay (uninstall the Store copy first, then install, then restart). `…` marks a command to type: keep it as it is. Settings → Apps → Installed apps is Windows 11's settings page: use Windows' own names for it in your language.

providers.codex.storePwsh.label.text: PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store is installed
providers.codex.storePwsh.label.note: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers (#585, #1404): the short label of the warning about the Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7 (a badge and the banner atop the window); the explanation follows under it.

providers.codex.storePwsh.symptom.text: The symptom: a Codex command fails at once with `CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 5` (access denied), and works again once every PowerShell 7 window and command is closed.
providers.codex.storePwsh.symptom.note: Provider Setup (#585), under the warning about the Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7: how the problem shows. `…` marks the error as Codex prints it: keep it as it is.

providers.codex.storePwsh.warning.text: Codex agents' commands can fail while a PowerShell 7 from the Microsoft Store is open: Codex's Windows sandbox can't start that PowerShell while another copy of it runs.
providers.codex.storePwsh.warning.note: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers (#585): a warning that Codex's commands fail (Windows) while the Microsoft Store's PowerShell 7, the one found first, is running anywhere, e.g. in a terminal. Codex is the coding agent's name.

providers.copilot.planNote.text: Copilot Free uses Auto only; choosing a model needs a paid plan.
providers.copilot.planNote.note: A note in Provider Setup under GitHub Copilot. Copilot Free is the plan's name; Auto is Copilot's model choice: keep both names.

providers.copilot.toolNames.text: This CLI names Combwork's tools "{server}-" and the tool: where Combwork says cw_inbox, call {server}-cw_inbox.
providers.copilot.toolNames.note: A line of Copilot's custom instructions (#1346 item 7): Copilot names an MCP server's tools <server>-<tool>. server: Combwork's MCP server's name (combwork). cw_inbox is a tool's name: keep it.

providers.copilot.updateAnyway.note: Provider Setup button: explicitly retry a failed WinGet Copilot update with --force, replacing the old package despite changed files.

providers.copilot.updateModified.text: WinGet could not remove the old Copilot package. Its installed files may have changed since WinGet installed them, often because Copilot updated itself. Update anyway asks WinGet to replace them with --force. Stop Copilot agents first.
providers.copilot.updateModified.note: Provider Setup after WinGet portable removal failed. The exit code can also mean other removal failures, so the cause is tentative. Update anyway is the adjacent button; keep WinGet, Copilot and --force unchanged.

providers.readiness.notInstalled.note: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: Combwork didn't find the coding agent's CLI. {provider} is its name (Claude Code).

providers.readiness.signedOut.note: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: the coding agent's CLI has no sign-in. {provider} is its name.

providers.readiness.update.note: Provider Setup and Settings → Providers: a newer version of the coding agent is out. {provider} is its name, {version} the version.

providers.settings.hooksOff.text: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} turns off all hooks (disableAllHooks). Combwork's hooks are how it knows what the agent is doing (its status, file locks, what it is told) and they carry its status line, so Combwork doesn't start an agent without them. Take disableAllHooks out of those settings, or remove the --settings from Extra arguments in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.hooksOff.note: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: its settings turn Claude Code's hooks off. {source} is inline (settings written in the argument itself) or file; {file} is the file's path as the user wrote it. Keep --settings, disableAllHooks and the setting names as they are; "Agent Settings" and "Settings → Claude Code" are where to change it, as Combwork shows them.

providers.settings.noFile.note: Why a settings file can't be read, after "can't be read:" in another message: it doesn't exist.

providers.settings.noValue.text: The last --settings in Extra arguments has no value. Give it a settings file or inline JSON (--settings '''<file or JSON>'''), or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.noValue.note: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: its extra arguments end with --settings and nothing after it. Keep --settings as it is, and the straight quotes around <file or JSON>: each three apostrophes show one (ICU); the words file or JSON may be translated; "Agent Settings" and "Settings → Claude Code" are where to change it, as Combwork shows them.

providers.settings.notAFile.note: Why a settings file can't be read, after "can't be read:" in another message: the path is a folder or a device.

providers.settings.notJson.text: The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments) isn't valid JSON ({why}). Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notJson.note: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: its settings file isn't JSON. {file} is its path; {why} is the JSON parser's own words (English). Keep --settings and JSON as they are.

providers.settings.notList.text: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} sets {key} to something other than a list, which stops Combwork's hooks reaching it. Make it a list ([ … ]) or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notList.note: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: a hook allowlist in its settings isn't a list. {key} is the setting's name. {source} is inline (settings written in the argument itself) or file; {file} is the file's path as the user wrote it. Keep --settings and the setting names as they are; "Agent Settings" and "Settings → Claude Code" are where to change it, as Combwork shows them. Keep [ … ] as it is.

providers.settings.notObject.text: {source, select, inline {The --settings in Extra arguments} other {The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments)}} isn't a settings object ('{ … }'). Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.notObject.note: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: its settings aren't an object. {source} is inline (settings written in the argument itself) or file; {file} is the file's path as the user wrote it. Keep --settings and the setting names as they are; "Agent Settings" and "Settings → Claude Code" are where to change it, as Combwork shows them. Keep { … } as it is.

providers.settings.tooLarge.text: it's over Claude Code's 2 MiB limit for settings files
providers.settings.tooLarge.note: Why a settings file can't be read, after "can't be read:" in another message: it is larger than Claude Code takes. Keep 2 MiB as it is.

providers.settings.unreadable.text: The settings file {file} (--settings in Extra arguments) can't be read: {why}. Fix it or remove it in Agent Settings or Settings → Claude Code.
providers.settings.unreadable.note: Starting a Claude Code agent is refused: the settings file in its extra arguments can't be read. {file} is its path; {why} is the reason ("there is no such file", "it isn't a file", or the system's own words). Keep --settings as it is.

providers.unknown.text: Unknown provider "{provider}". It may need a newer version of Combwork.
providers.unknown.note: An agent or a setting names a coding-agent CLI this version of Combwork doesn't know, as when a newer Combwork wrote it. {provider} is the id.
